spots.name: Cathedral of Saint Mother Teresa
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saint Mother Teresa is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Pristina, Kosovo. In 2007, the Government of Kosovo approved plans for the building. The cathedral is dedicated to the Albanian-Indian Roman Catholic nun and missionary Saint Teresa of Calcutta.

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The National Library of Kosovo is the highest library institution in Kosovo established by the Assembly and is located in Pristina.

spots.summary: The Gračanica Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery located in Kosovo. It was built by the Serbian king Stefan Milutin in 1321.

spots.name: Bill Clinton Boulevard
spots.summary: Bill Clinton Boulevard is a boulevard located in Pristina, Kosovo. Following the Kosovo War of 1998 to 1999, Albanians in Kosovo wanted to thank former U.S. President Bill Clinton for his help in their struggle with the government of Yugoslavia.

spots.name: Newborn monument
spots.summary: The Newborn Monument (NEWBORN) is a typographic sculpture and tourist attraction in Pristina, Kosovo. Located in front of the Palace of Youth and Sports, the monument was unveiled on 17 February 2008, the day that Kosovo formally declared its independence from Serbia.

spots.name: Kosovo Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Kosovo Museum is the national museum of Kosovo, located in the city of Pristina. Established by Yugoslav authorities in 1949, this is the largest museum in Kosovo. It is situated in a 1889 Austro-Hungarian-style building, formerly used as the high military command headquarters.

spots.name: King Mosque, Pristina

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Imperial Mosque, also known as King's Mosque, is an Ottoman mosque located in Pristina, Kosovo. It was built in 1461 by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror.

names.ja: ファティスルタンメフメットモスク

spots.name: Skanderbeg Square, Pristina
spots.summary: Skanderbeg Square is a square in Pristina, Kosovo.

spots.name: Christ the Saviour Cathedral
spots.summary: The Cathedral church of Christ the Saviour in Pristina, Kosovo, is an unfinished Serbian Orthodox Christian church whose construction began in 1992. Due to have been completed in 1999, its construction, on the campus of the pre-war University of Pristina, was interrupted by the Kosovo War.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Christ the Saviour, Pristina

spots.name: Çarshi Mosque
spots.summary: The Çarshi Mosque, also known as the Bazaar Mosque and the Taş Mosque, is the oldest building in Pristina, Kosovo, and it marks the beginning of the old town.

spots.name: Jashar Pasha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jashar Pasha Mosque is a historical mosque in Pristina, Kosovo. The mosque was built in 1834 by the mayor of Skopje, Mehmet Yasar.

spots.name: Heroinat Memorial
spots.summary: The Heroinat Memorial (HEROINAT) (Albanian: Memoriali Heroinat) is a typographic sculpture and tourist attraction in Pristina, Kosovo. The memorial is placed in a park in downtown Pristina, in one of Prishtina's most central and frequented areas, in front of Newborn monument.

spots.name: National Gallery of Kosovo

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The National Gallery of Kosovo, formerly known as the Kosova National Art Gallery, is an art gallery situated at the University of Pristina Campus that focuses on 20th-century art.

spots.name: Germia Park
spots.summary: Germia Park is a regional park located in the northeast of Pristina, Kosovo, and covers an area of 62 square kilometres (24 sq mi). Its highest point, Butos Peak, is 1050 meters above sea level and its lowest 663 meters above sea level.

spots.name: Clock Tower of Pristina
spots.summary: The Clock Tower in Pristina, Kosovo, was built in the 19th century by Jashar Pasha, after whom the Mosque is named not far from the Clock Tower. It served as a means of informing the town during the Ottoman Empire rule, in order to let people know when to pray as well as the traders closing their shops.

spots.name: National Theatre of Kosovo
spots.summary: The National Theatre of Kosovo was founded in 1946 in the city of Prizren, Kosovo. It is the highest ranked theatre institution in the country, with the largest number of productions. The National Theatre is the only public theatre in Kosovo and therefore it is financed by Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sport.

spots.name: Ethnological Museum, Pristina

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Ethnological Treasure of Kosovo is an ethnographic museum in Pristina, Kosovo. It is located in the Emin Gjiku Complex, a monument of culture from the 18th century. The house was once owned by the family of Emin Gjikolli.

spots.name: Fadil Vokrri Stadium
spots.summary: The Fadil Vokrri Stadium, previously known as Pristina City Stadium, is a multi-purpose stadium in Pristina, Kosovo, which is used mostly for football matches and is the home ground of FC Prishtina and the Kosovo national football team. The stadium has a capacity of 13,980.

names.es: Estadio de la Ciudad de Pristina

spots.name: Shadërvan
spots.summary: Shadërvan is a marble fountain located between the Çarshi Mosque and the Museum of Kosovo in Pristina, Kosovo, and is a typical component of Ottoman architecture. The fountain is the only one remaining in the city from over fifty that once existed.

spots.name: Monument of Brotherhood and Unity, Pristina
Elena Gjika Elementary School
spots.summary: The Elena Gjika Elementary School is a cultural heritage monument in Pristina, Kosovo, and one of the oldest intact buildings in the entire city.

spots.name: Приштинска синагога

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Galeria 17 is in the old neighborhood of Pristina. With a distinct focus on social issues, artists and curators are invited to experiment with concepts, ideas and space. The gallery exhibits content that creates dialogue and fosters public debate while contributing to the documentation and creation of missing references throughout a process that archives and educates.

spots.name: Pristina Archives
spots.summary: The Pristina Archives is a cultural heritage monument in Pristina, Kosovo.

spots.name: Q77193161
spots.summary: It was designed by the Serbian sculptor Miodrag Zirkovic in 1957 and built in 1959. The Brotherhood and Unity monument was constructed during a time of major changes in the capital of Kosovo. The Yugoslav authorities brought a new spirit of socialist realism, which was also manifested through architecture.

spots.name: Hotel Union in Prishtina
spots.summary: The building of the former “Hotel Union” was built in 1927 under the supervision of the Austrian architect, Andrija Kremer. It combined elements of neo-Renaissance, neo-baroque and Art Nouveau and was one of the few buildings in Pristina with European-architecture influence. hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palace of Youth and Sports is a remarkable structure – a symbol for the city of Prishtina – where many activities are held throughout the year. The complex is a popular meeting spot, a stage, a place for cultivating talents and a site that shapes the city’s identity.The decision to build the Palace of Youth and Sports was made by a public referendum. spots.name: City Park
spots.summary: City park is one of the few parks that city has. It is 500 m from the city centre, about a 7-minute walk. Park has 7.5 hectares, rich flora and fauna, fresh air, hiking trails arranged in the beautiful nature, surrounded but pines and other trees. Hidden from center and heavy traffic and pollution, it is perfect place for escaping and spending quality time with family, friends. During late spring

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Rron Restaurant is just outside the Pristina city limits on the way to Gracanica. Hidden behind an under-construction building for the past couple of years as of 2025, it is popular with local and international politicians as well as ordinary people. spots.name: Soma Book Station

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Upscale institution, popular both by day and night. Known for their carefully curated in-house bookshop, including vinyls and the products of local artists, as well as evening musical performances across all genres, Soma acquaints their guests with quality literature, art and music. Exposed-brick walls with trendy light fixtures and a vaulted ceiling creates a warm indoor atmosphere with a careful

spots.name: Miqt Pub
spots.summary: Cozy and cool interior that feels more like a proper expat pub, however it is frequented by locals. The garden is decorated with artwork and neon lights that give it an inviting feel by night. The pub has a full bar and menu and the staff is friendly and helpful. The pub hosts regular events and DJs in the evening. It is a great central place to relax or start your night before hitting the clubs.

spots.name: 13 Rooftop

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Pristina's first Rooftop Lounge Bar, overlooking a 360-degree view of its skyline. Has two connected venues: a fully enclosed ‘Penthouse Lounge’ and a fully outfitted ‘Sway Bar/Club.’ It also encloses 4 outdoor Rooftop Gardens, each with a different view of the city, and 1 outdoor heated smoking venue. There is typically a cover charge for men.

spots.name: Pristina Hackerspace Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The bar is open every Wednesday nights starting from 17:30 catering to the tech community. Hand crafted beer is available for €2 (2025). The staff and regulars are always welcoming, and the proceeds from the bar go to support the community at Hackerspace.

spots.name: Zanzi Jazz Bar

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: This bar in a basement right off of the main pedestrian boulevard has live dance music every night. The house band performs covers songs of hits from around the world. Every Monday Zanzi has an open mic night and karaoke with a live band.

spots.name: Piccadilly – Burektore
spots.summary: Family business that sells delicious, cheap burek. The types of burek that are served are with meat and cheese, preferably eaten with yoghurt or ayran. Try to engage in a conversation, as the owner/server is quite a character.

spots.name: Pi Shat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is a traditional Albanian restaurant with a wonderful atmosphere. If you are unfamiliar with Albanian food, just ask the waiters to put together a platter for you - you'll end up with a delicious range of grilled meats.

spots.name: Ciao

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This Macedonian restaurant on the road out of town to Skopje and Gracaniza is a popular stop for internationals and aid workers craving a bacon-wrapped pork medallion, or some of the best bread and salad in the city.

spots.name: Marcus Coffee Shop
spots.summary: Serves locally roasted beans which are also available for sale in-house. Producing both Turkish and espresso-based styles of coffee, the staff will happily chat about the origins of their blends.

spots.name: Duplex Premium

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Slightly pretentious but staple club. Fills up throughout the year and is styled for Pristina's pop and rap scene. The club has a dress code, so be sure to look smart when you go.

spots.name: Pinocchio restaurant and hotel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Excellent food and a warm atmosphere, as well as a panoramic view of Pristina below. For lunch, hit Te Komiteti on Qamil Hoxha street and have the gazpacho and chicken sandwich.

spots.name: Renaissance Restaurant

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: A traditional restaurant with great food and service, all for a flat fee, which includes several small dishesh, a main dish, and unlimited wine, rakija and beers.

spots.name: Tillt Radio / Vinyl Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Laid-back vinyl bar, playing lounge, garage, soul and other smooths tunes. Popular with the young crowd. Well worth the long walk and across the rail track.

spots.name: Liburnia Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A great opportunity to taste Kosovar cuisine in an evocative environment full of plants. Meat recommended. The waiters are kind and helpful.

spots.name: Soma Slow Food
spots.summary: It offers several standard menus of traditional foods with a modern twist. People that have visited remain in two minds about it.

spots.name: Aurora

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lovely place, plenty to offer. Very helpful and understanding staff. Comfortable place to have your meals.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Located along the Mother Theresa Boulevard, it's one of the most famous Burek places in Pristina.

spots.name: Amadeus

spots.summary: Another restaurant in the Dragodan neighborhood. Serves pizza and other western dishes.
